entries.appliesTo: operators who develop and make a conversational AI service available to the public

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 554J.2(1) — 'An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to a minor account holder that the minor account holder is interacting with artificial intelligence'; § 554J.3 — 'An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose using a persistent visible disclaimer, or a disclaimer that appears after every three hours of continuous interaction with the operator's conversational AI service, that the operator's conversational AI service is artificial intelligence if a reasonable individual interacting with the conversational AI service would believe that the individual is interacting with a human'
dutySources.content-safeguards: § 554J.2(3) — 'An operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the operator's conversational AI service from doing any of the following for minor account holders: a. Producing visual depictions of sexually explicit material'; § 554J.2(4) — 'An operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the operator's conversational AI service from generating statements that would lead a reasonable individual to believe that the individual is interacting with a human'
dutySources.crisis-protocol: § 554J.4 — 'An operator shall adopt protocols for the operator's conversational AI service for responding to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self-harm that includes but is not limited to making reasonable efforts to refer the user to crisis service providers'

sources.scope: § 554J.1(2)(a) — '"Conversational AI service" means an artificial intelligence, available by software application, web interface, or computer program, that is accessible to the general public and that has the primary purpose of simulating human conversation and interaction through text, audio communication, or visual communication'
sources.ageFocus: §§ 554J.3–554J.5 bind operators as to any user (§ 554J.4 — 'responding to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self-harm'); § 554J.2 adds minor-specific requirements ('Conversational AI services —— minors —— requirements')
sources.aiDisclosure: § 554J.2(1)(b)(2) — 'A disclaimer that appears at least once every three hours of continuous interaction between the operator's conversational AI service and a minor account holder'; § 554J.3 — 'a persistent visible disclaimer, or a disclaimer that appears after every three hours of continuous interaction'
sources.crisisProtocol: § 554J.4 — 'making reasonable efforts to refer the user to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis service'
sources.parentalTools: § 554J.2(5)(b) — 'An operator shall offer tools for the parent or guardian of a minor account holder to manage the minor account holder's privacy and account settings if the minor is under thirteen years of age'
sources.engagementLimits: § 554J.2(2) — 'An operator shall not provide a minor user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with the intent to encourage increased engagement with the operator's conversational AI service'
sources.contentSafeguards: § 554J.2(3) — 'An operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the operator's conversational AI service from doing any of the following for minor account holders: a. Producing visual depictions of sexually explicit material. b. Stating that the minor account holder should engage in sexually explicit conduct. c. Sexually objectifying the minor account holder.'
sources.ageThreshold: § 554J.1(3) — '"Minor" means an individual an operator knows is, or is reasonably certain is, under eighteen years of age'
sources.penaltyMax: § 554J.6(1)(b) — 'A civil penalty of one thousand dollars per violation, up to a maximum of five hundred thousand dollars per operator'
sources.enforcer: § 554J.6(2) — 'The attorney general shall have the authority to enforce this chapter'; § 554J.6(4) — 'This chapter shall not be construed to create a private right of action under this chapter or any other law'

exposure.penaltyUnit: aggregate cap per operator ($1,000 per violation)

flags: remedy structure: operator 'shall be subject to an injunction and liable for the greater of' actual damages or the civil penalty (§ 554J.6(1)) — actual damages have no stated cap; penalties deposited into state general fund (§ 554J.6(3))
developer safe harbor: no liability 'solely because a third party used the developer's artificial intelligence model to create or train a conversational AI service' (§ 554J.6(5))

§ 554J.5 prohibits an operator from knowingly programming the service to make representations 'that the conversational AI service is designed to provide professional psychology or behavioral health services that an individual would require licensure under chapter 154B or 154D to provide' — conduct prohibition with no matching duty key (borders mental-health-practice family but is a single prohibition within the same operator-facing chapter, not segmented)

scope enum lossy: 'conversational AI service' is broader than companion apps but § 554J.1(2)(b) excludes research tools, embedded features, narrow-topic bots, business customer-service bots, voice assistants, and internal business tools — 'all-chatbots' chosen as closest

ageFocus enum lossy: § 554J.2 duties (rewards ban, content safeguards, human-impersonation safeguards, parental/privacy tools) bind only as to minor account holders; §§ 554J.3–554J.5 apply to all users — 'all-users' chosen as closest

aiDisclosure enum lossy: statute allows either 'A persistent visible disclaimer' or a disclaimer 'at the beginning of each interaction' plus 'at least once every three hours of continuous interaction' for minors (§ 554J.2(1)); for all users, persistent or every-three-hours disclaimer required only 'if a reasonable individual...would believe that the individual is interacting with a human' (§ 554J.3) — 'periodic' chosen as closest

parental tools tiering: mandatory parent/guardian tools 'if the minor is under thirteen years of age' (§ 554J.2(5)(b)); for other minors only 'as appropriate based on relevant risks' (§ 554J.2(5)(c)); minors themselves must get privacy/account tools (§ 554J.2(5)(a))

§ 554J.2(4) safeguards against human-impersonation include preventing 'Explicit claims that the conversational AI service is sentient or human', 'Statements that simulate emotional dependence on a minor account holder', romantic/sexual-innuendo simulation, and 'Role-playing an adult-minor romantic relationship' — coded under content-safeguards
no age-assurance duty: 'Minor' turns on what the operator 'knows is, or is reasonably certain is' — no verification requirement stated
rulemaking: attorney general 'shall adopt rules pursuant to chapter 17A to administer this chapter' (§ 554J.6(2))
